event: First anomaly: caseload +6.7%, but attributable to 16-25 age extension (school-age -0.3%). Genuinely ambiguous.
THE PIVOT: caseload +12.1% (36 sigma above 2014 planning assumption); school-age growth positive; new plans +24% above any statements-era year. Low-regret window opens.
First S251 outturn trend: independent top-ups ~£1bn, rising 8%/yr.
Statutory transition ends: conversion can no longer explain growth.
Caseload +11.3% (60 sigma); new plans +45% above statements-era peak. Window for capital decisions.
FIRST RESPONSE: £250m revenue top-up + £100m capital over two years (~4% of high-needs budget/yr); call for evidence.
Caseload +10.7% (86 sigma); extrapolation now predicts 2024 within 1%. NAO report (Sept) and Education Committee (Oct) publish the diagnosis.
SEND Review launched. Spending round adds >£700m high-needs revenue for 2020-21 (demand-following). First modest EP training expansion announced: intake ~160 to ~200/yr from Sept 2020 (qualify 2023).
DSG statutory override: deficits moved off council balance sheets (accounting measure, no capacity).
Safety Valve programme begins: bespoke deficit-recovery deals (38 councils by 2024, >£1bn of DfE payments).
SEND green paper. FIRST MAJOR CAPITAL PROGRAMME: £2.6bn high-needs capital 2022-25 (announced SR21) - the 2018-window decision, four years late; places land 2024-27.
SEND & AP Improvement Plan: workforce plan, quality standards. £21m for 2024+2025 EP cohorts (~400/yr intake from Sept 2024; qualify 2027+).
Safety Valve closed to new entrants. Cumulative DSG deficits >£3.3bn; override extended to March 2026.
White paper: structural redesign of the 2014 framework.
